A.claim: A read-only API key can delete a check via DELETE /api/vN/checks/<uuid>, because delete_check accepts read-only keys (authorize_read).

The check listing endpoint GET /api/vN/checks/ (get_checks) filters by the project's owner instead of the key's project, so a key for one project lists checks (and, with a read-write key, their uuid and ping URLs) of the owner's other projects.

GET /api/vN/checks/<unique_key> (get_check_by_unique_key) returns the full check details (uuid, ping_url, update/pause/resume URLs, channels) to a read-only key because it does not pass the read-only flag to to_dict.
The pings, ping body and channels endpoints reject the read-only key (authorize), which may deny read access the read-only key is meant to have.

The authorize decorator accepts the API key from the JSON request body on POST, in addition to the header.
